images.filename: Toronto First Chinatown Plaque 2 - Nathan Phillips Square Toronto ON ON M5H 2N1, Canada.jpg
images.caption: This first Chinatown thrived until the late 1940s, when the City of Toronto began its controversial expropriation of much of the neighbourhood to make room for a new city hall and the future Nathan Phillips Square. Demolition finally took place in 1955. Some Chinese businesses could not afford to re-locate, and closed. Others packed up and moved west along Dundas Street to Spadina Avenue where they became the heart of today's 'Old Chinatown'.
